_comment: *** THIS FILE IS A FORMAT TEMPLATE AND IS NOT EVIDENCE. ***
It contains NO real review. Its 'reviewer' is an illustrative placeholder, and
jev-arbiter-review.py REFUSES it with exit 1 rather than emitting an
AGREES/DISAGREES verdict from filler. To use it, copy it, replace 'reviewer'
with a real identity, and set dataset_sha256 to the capture you are reviewing.
What the tool decides by the CHOSEN REFERENCE, not by rank:
selected_candidate  IS the incumbent
legal_alternatives[n] is by definition NOT what the game took
Rank is deliberately NOT used for the verdict: two different proposals can
score identically, and a rank-based verdict would report AGREEMENT for a
challenger that picked a different objective.
These are NOT produced by the shadow recorder and NOT inferred by the tool.
Both envelopes are REFUSED unless bound: dataset_sha256 must equal the
capture's own sha256, and every cycle_id must exist in the capture and be
unique. The tool binds the DECLARATION to the capture; it does NOT open or
verify the cited source file, so source provenance remains a human reviewer's
responsibility, not something this tool validates.
Benefit is ALWAYS UNKNOWN: no artifact observes what the other candidate would
have produced, so a DISAGREES verdict is a difference of opinion, not an
improvement. No Jev model produced any of this; no model caller is configured
in this repository.
reviewer: EXAMPLE-REVIEWER (illustrative; replace with a real identity)

critique.claim: I would have taken the legal AcceptQuest instead of the priority-30 TurnInQuest on this wake.
critique.basis: Reviewer opinion on the frozen candidate set. No postcondition in this dataset measures which pick was worth more, so this states a preference only.

critique.claim: I agree the AcceptQuest incumbent was right here; the turn-in wake is no longer competing.
critique.basis: Reviewer opinion; picks the incumbent, which must compare as AGREES.
